description:
Adds the `gf2-sim` tests that a checkpointed campaign with a batch-decoding stage resumes to the results of an uninterrupted run.

## Background

The batch soft-decoder trait of `gf2-coding` decodes a batch of LLR frames into caller-provided decoded words and per-frame outcomes in input order. Its LDPC implementer, the LDPC batch decoder, decodes fixed waves of eight lanes with per-frame termination, routes a wave to the lane kernels or to the single-frame decoder by the decode selectors of the coding tuning section, and returns each frame's result equal to the single-frame decoder's bit for bit as `docs/reference/ldpc-decoder-numerical-contract.md` states. The CPU LDPC, 5G NR and DVB-T2 decode stages of `gf2-sim` decode their batches through it. A frame's result depends on its own LLRs alone, so no grouping of frames into waves changes it; the simulation layer adds worker scheduling and checkpointed campaigns on top, and determinism there is asserted, not inferred. The suite `checkpoint_compat` interrupts a checkpointed SNR point and compares the resumed counters with an uninterrupted reference.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: A campaign with a batch-decoding stage, interrupted at a checkpoint and resumed, produces counters byte-identical to an uninterrupted run, at one, two and four workers.
- [hard] REQ-02: The batch size puts a checkpoint boundary inside a decode wave.
- [hard] REQ-03: Each test meets the fast-tier budget or carries a descriptive simulation-tier ignore reason.
title: Show checkpoint resume identity of batch-decoding campaigns
